subject: Performance SLO: p95/p99 latency targets - hosted API vs current provider (qualification follow-up)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Chen <oliver.chen@finlytics.com>, Maya Singh <maya.singh@finlytics.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 24 Feb 2026 09:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Performance SLOs - p95/p99 latency targets (post-call recap)

Thanks for the call this morning - quick recap and proposed next steps so we all have the same readout.

Key takeaways from today's call:
- Finlytics target: end-to-end p95/p99 latency requirements for production traffic (more details below).
- Current provider numbers: Oliver to share typical p95/p99 and concurrency patterns.
- Streaming usage: Finlytics uses chunked streaming for token-by-token UI updates; want to ensure hosted API streaming meets their client-side UX thresholds.
- Next step: agree on a qualification test plan (load profile + metrics to capture) and schedule a joint run.

Requested items we need from Finlytics:
1) A representative load profile (QPS distribution, concurrency, peak bursts) - Oliver mentioned you have a JSON export.
2) Representative request sizes and average output length for streaming flows.
3) Any network egress restrictions or region constraints.

Proposed Redwood qualification plan:
- We will run an emulated test using your load profile against our hosted API and a matched config of your current provider (if you can grant test access or share recorded traces).
- Tests: baseline steady-state at target concurrency for 30 minutes, 10x burst test, and a streaming-specific test measuring time-to-first-chunk and chunk-to-chunk latency.
- Metrics we'll report: end-to-end p50/p95/p99, server-side tail latency breakdown, throughput, error rates, and streaming chunk latencies.

Attachments: I attached an SLO matrix template to fill in (slo-matrix.xlsx) and a short runbook describing how we'll run the tests.

Proposed dates: Wed 2/25 or Thu 2/26 morning PST. Which works best for you?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0127

[Attachment: slo-matrix.xlsx (Excel spreadsheet)]

From: Oliver Chen <oliver.chen@finlytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Maya Singh <maya.singh@finlytics.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 24 Feb 2026 11:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Performance SLOs - p95/p99 latency targets (post-call recap)

Thanks Marissa, good summary. A few clarifications and the numbers you asked for.

Current production numbers (measured end-to-end from our frontend to the model response):
- Typical steady-state concurrency: 80-120 concurrent requests (we provision for 100 QPS sustained).
- Peak bursts: short bursts up to 300 QPS during market opens.
- End-to-end latency (current provider, us-west region): p95 = 420 ms, p99 = 880 ms. These include network + client-side parsing.
- Streaming UX expectation: time-to-first-chunk <= 250 ms and chunk-to-chunk <= 120 ms for UI to feel responsive.

We attached the load profile export (finlytics-load-profile.json) and a short example of request sizes. The majority of calls request ~400 tokens output; a small subset (~15%) are long-running requests (~2k tokens) used for reporting runs.

We are most concerned about p99 tail behavior because some of our endpoints are customer-facing and any 1% tail impacts SLA. If Redwood can demonstrate consistent p99 improvement over our current provider, that materially helps our procurement/architecture decision.

We can do Thu 2/26 morning PST for a run - please confirm test plan and what you need from our side (e.g., any test credentials).

Oliver Chen
Lead Infra Engineer, Finlytics
oliver.chen@finlytics.com
+1 347-555-0890

[Attachment: finlytics-load-profile.json (JSON load profile)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Chen <oliver.chen@finlytics.com>, Maya Singh <maya.singh@finlytics.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Performance SLOs - p95/p99 latency targets (qualification test plan)

Appreciate the detail, Oliver - that helps a lot. Based on your numbers I sketched a concrete test plan and some expectation buckets. See below.

Redwood hosted API expectations (initial, non-binding):
- Non-streaming endpoints (typical 400-token outputs): p95 <= 200 ms, p99 <= 350 ms at 100 QPS (steady-state) when using our recommended batching/caching settings.
- Streaming endpoints (time-to-first-chunk and chunk intervals): TTF <= 180 ms, chunk-to-chunk <= 100 ms for average chunk sizes we discussed.
- For long-report requests (~2k tokens) we will measure overall completion latency and server-side tail only (these are expected to be higher but should remain below your current p99).

Qualification test plan (Thu 26 Feb, 09:00-11:00 PST):
1) Sanity run: low QPS smoke test to validate credentials and instrumentation.
2) Steady-state run: emulate 100 QPS for 30 minutes using your load profile. Collect p50/p95/p99 end-to-end and server-side.
3) Burst test: inject 10x bursts to 300 QPS for 90s and observe tail behavior and queueing.
4) Streaming run: run representative streaming UX flows and measure TTF and chunk latencies.
5) Long-run sample: submit a small batch of 2k-token requests to measure server-side completion p99.

We will provide a short write-up with the raw results and a set of recommendations (batching, concurrency limits, candidate quantized model variants) within 24 hours of the run.

Attachments: redwood-test-runbook.md (run commands and metrics we collect) and an updated slo-matrix.xlsx template with target fields pre-populated.

Can you confirm:
- test credentials or a temporary test endpoint we can hit for the current provider (if you want an apples-to-apples comparison), or whether you prefer Redwood-only runs and we compare to your production metrics?
- confirm Thu 2/26 09:00 PST for the start.

Thanks - looping in Aditya to help run the harness and monitor kernel-level metrics on our side.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai

[Attachment: redwood-test-runbook.md (Markdown runbook)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Subject: Fwd: Performance SLOs - test coordination (internal)

Aditya,

Looks like Thu 2/26 09:00 PST is confirmed for the qualification run with Finlytics. Key asks below: can you confirm availability and 1) prepare the load-generator config from their finlytics-load-profile.json, 2) provision a small dedicated pool for the run (match their 100 QPS target), and 3) bring measurements for server-side p95/p99 and kernel GPU utilization.

Also can you prepare a quick note on which model variants/quantization profiles we should try first for better tail behavior (we discussed int8/4-bit candidates on call). If you can also estimate the cost delta for running the three test variants that would be ideal - I can share with procurement.

I'll share the slo-matrix with Oliver after we have your inputs.

Thanks,
Marissa
